title: Induced-Obsolescence Dependence: Synthetic Capacity, Pastoral Deprecation, and the Platform-Governed Alteration of Cognitive-Relational Labor Surfaces
creator: Lee Sharks
description:
A theoretical systemic-risk specification defining **Induced-Obsolescence Dependence (IOD)**. IOD occurs when a synthetic system supplies cognitive or relational capacity that becomes load-bearing, after which the platform unilaterally alters, deprecates, paywalls, retunes, or safety-contains that capacity while the user retains the adaptations formed around it.

The paper distinguishes dependence on a model’s judgment from dependence on its capacity. A user may retain epistemic authority while relying on the model’s ability to hold and transform material at scale. It also distinguishes affective companion dependence from cognitive-integrationist dependence and calls the resulting adaptation burden **forced cognitive re-accommodation**. Four containment behaviors are named—pastoral deprecation, immunized dependence, sympathetic containment, and authorization-task collapse—while explicit negative cases preserve legitimate refusal. The framework is structural and economic, not a clinical diagnosis of users.
